title: Regional fallbacks, split-brain mitigation and contract-aware throttling
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a pragmatic architecture for combining region-aware routing, control-plane coordination, and contract-aware throttling. Goal: ensure customer SLAs are honored at a global level while minimizing split-brain behavior during regional control-plane outages and providing deterministic, auditable degradation paths for noisy neighbors.

Context and motivation:
- We operate global inference endpoints with low-latency regional affinity. Customers pin contracts (SLA tiers) and may have reserved capacity (Dedicated) or shared-hosted usage.
- Two classes of failures cause the worst UX: (1) regional capacity pressure causing unfair eviction of important customers; (2) partial control-plane partition that leads different regions to apply contradictory routing/eviction decisions (split-brain).
- This doc sketches a hybrid control-plane model, per-tenant local heuristics, and a contract-first throttling policy that degrade gracefully and are easy to audit.

Key principles (short):
1) Contract-first: any global decision must preserve higher-tier customer commitments unless impossible (explicit fallbacks).
2) Local safety with global reconciliation: region-level controllers make fast decisions using locally-available signals; a background global reconciler corrects drift and resolves conflicts post-hoc.
3) Deterministic degradation: define a ranked set of degradation actions (cache eviction, quantized model downgrade, latency-optimized routing, per-tenant throttling, hard eject) with clear billing/notification consequences.
4) Observable & reversible: every action emits an audit event with reason, affected tenant(s), metrics snapshot, and counterfactual (what would have happened if not taken).

Actors and surfaces:
- Edge router (region): routes incoming requests; has per-tenant sticky affinity token but can fall back.
- Regional control-plane: holds recent quotas, local usage, and policy (30s heartbeat granularity). Makes immediate admission decisions and local evictions.
- Global control-plane (active in a region or multi-master): stores canonical contracts, long-term quotas, and coordinates cross-region relocations. Runs reconciliation tasks and escalation workflows.
- Billing/Account service: authoritative source for contract tiers and reserved capacity commitments; exposes read-only caches to regional controllers.

Signals available to regional controller (local, fast):
- qps and token consumption (1s, 10s windows)
- GPU utilization and concurrency queue depth
- KV cache hit ratio and prefix cache memory usage
- Recent retry/error spike (5s–1m)
- Synthetic SLO p50/p95 observed from probes
- Local reserved pool footprint (allocations currently landed)

Global signals (eventual):
- Contract overrides, newly-applied credits/penalties
- Cross-region replication backlog and migrating session tokens
- Global capacity map and known outages

Decision model (high level):
1) Admission check: region receives request with tenant_id and desired model. It validates token and reads local cached contract snapshot (TTL ~ 20s). If cache missing, allow short-circuit: allow small number of requests while fetching fallback (optimistic allow with sampled audit).
2) Fast policy: if local reserved capacity available for tenant => admit. Else evaluate cost function: 
   score = alpha*(tenant_priority) + beta*(remaining_quota_fraction) - gamma*(current_queue_depth)
   - tenant_priority derived from SLA: platinum=100, gold=70, silver=40, free=0
   - remaining_quota_fraction approx remaining_tokens/committed_tokens
   - coefficients tuned per-region
3) Degradation ladder (apply in order until admission succeeds or request rejected):
   a) fast-path: reuse cached KV prefix or local reroute to warm replica (no billing change)
   b) apply micro-throttle (burst allowed; sustained throttling blocks): slow responses but partial success
   c) model-quality downgrade (apply narrow quantized model or shorter context); record explicit warning to downstream
   d) enqueue with longer deadline and background continuation (best-effort)
   e) hard reject (429) — only when contract forbids fallback or on explicit eviction list

Split-brain mitigation and tie-break rules:
- Problem: two regions lose connectivity and independently decide to evict tenant X and tenant Y — both high-value. When connection recovers, naive reconcile may find both were evicted and both claim capacity.
- Approach: optimistic local decisions + time-bounded leases. When regional controller evicts or reassigns reserved capacity, it writes a signed lease event to local durable log and broadcasts a compact lease delta to peers. Leases have: tenant_id, region, lease_start, lease_expiry, signed_seq. If peers are unreachable, lease is still valid until expiry (short by design, e.g., 90s).
- On reconnection, the global reconciler applies deterministic sorting: 1) leases with latest signed_seq win; 2) ties broken by contract priority; 3) if still tied, prefer region with lower global load metric.
- Forced arbitration: if global control-plane cannot reconcile safely (contradictions and both regions currently saturated), trigger emergency-preserve-mode: freeze all new allocations for affected tenants and route traffic to read-only fallback model. Notify SRE and account team.

Contract-aware throttling (detail):
- Every contract defines: committed_tokens_per_window, burst_tokens, min_latency_slo, reserved_capacity_flag (true for Dedicated), notification_policy (email + webhook), financial_penalty_clause (yes/no).
- Throttle decisions consult both local usage and global committed tokens from account service cache. For shared-hosted tenants without reservation, policy biases throttles earlier than for reserved customers.
- Implementation sketch: each tenant has a local token-bucket mirror. When admitted, pre-decrement mirror immediately and enqueue a reliable decrement event to the global ledger (append-only). If ledger cannot be reached, regional mirror continues until safe margin (e.g., 5% overcommit) then starts shedding gracefully.

Noisy neighbor detection and remediation:
- Signals: sudden rise in per-tenant per-model latency, persistent queue growth for tenant's sessions, exponential retry cascades from downstream services, cache churn > 20%/min.
- Heuristics to spot noisy tenants: (a) cross-tenant correlation windows where one tenant's increase aligns with others' degradation; (b) high model hotset turnover; (c) repeated autoscaling churn beyond expected pattern.
- Remediation steps (prefer non-disruptive first):
  1) Inject micro-throttle for offending tenant (10–30s windows) + notify customer via webhook
  2) Move noisy tenant to isolated capacity pool (if on Dedicated or burst pools exist) — automatic for customers with reserved pool; for shared, create opt-in isolation with billing review
  3) If still noisy: schedule model-eviction from shared KV caches and force hard partition for 60s while metrics stabilize

Observability and auditability requirements:
- Every routing decision emits: event_id, timestamp, tenant_id, region, reason_code, metrics snapshot (qps, queue_depth, util), previous_action, resulting_action, humans_notified flag. Events retained for 90 days (hot) then archived.
- Expose per-tenant routing timeline in console with links to raw events and easy-to-read human summary (why were you throttled, when will you be back to normal?).

Reconciliation and eventual consistency windows:
- Regional controllers make short-lived leasing decisions with expiry 60–120s depending on region latency. Global reconciler runs every 30s to 2m depending on cross-region sync health and escalates if drift > threshold (e.g., >5% of reserved allocations inconsistent).
- Safe replays: reconciliation must be idempotent; operations are expressed as CRDT-ish deltas with monotonic sequence numbers per tenant to avoid lost updates.

Operational playbook (brief):
- On region partial control-plane outage:
  1) Regional controllers switch to local-only mode (continue serving using cached contracts; extend leases by local_policy_ttl)
  2) Increase observability sampling and emit partition events to ops channel
  3) If local queue depth crosses critical threshold: apply contract-first throttles and run noisy-neighbor heuristics
  4) When control-plane recovers: run reconciliation; if conflicts, follow tie-break rules and, if unclear, run emergency-preserve-mode and paginates SRE/account

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: Prototype in staging for two regions with synthetic noisy-tenant scenarios. Validate lease expiry and deterministic reconciliation.
- Phase 1: Canary in low-traffic region for non-reserved customers; monitor false-positive throttles for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2: Gradual expansion to all regions; add Dedicated path testing where tenant reservations are exercised end-to-end.
- Phase 3: Enable full console visibility and tenant-facing notifications.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- Lease length: shorter leases reduce split-brain window but increase cross-region chatter under flakey networks. 90s felt like a pragmatic default — need stress tests.
- Overcommit policy: how much global overcommit to allow for optimistic fast-paths? 2–5% vs 10% has different customer expectation profiles.
- Billing semantics during degradations: if we downgrade quality (quantized model) do we bill full tokens? Need legal/product alignment.

Action items / next steps:
- Build staging harness that can simulate control-plane partitions and noisy tenants (owner: Noah; EOD 2026-03-15).
- Prototype lease event format and reconciliation algorithm (owner: Sofia; prototype PR).
- Draft notification wording and console UI for per-tenant routing timeline (owner: Priya).
- Schedule tabletop incident to exercise emergency-preserve-mode (owner: Arjun; target 2026-04-01).

Appendix: example audit event (single-line json-ready for logs)
{"event_id":"evt-20260301-0001","ts":"2026-03-01T12:01:23Z","tenant":"tenant-237","region":"us-west-2","reason":"local_capacity_pressure","action":"micro_throttle","prev":"admit","qps":132.4,"queue_depth":37}

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and tradeoff-oriented. Looking for feedback on lease TTLs, scoring coefficients, and billing implications of model downgrades.
- If you have product/legal constraints that would change degradation ladder or billing behavior, call them out explicitly in comments or Confluence link above.
